newsitem.title: USA: Material says accounting problems isolated.
newsitem.headline: Material says accounting problems isolated.

text.p: Material Sciences Corp said an investigation showed that a former plant controller acted alone and was solely reponsible for certain accounting irregularities.
"We are also undertaking a complete review of our internal accounting controls," said chief executive Gerald Nadig.

Expenses associated with the probe will hurt first quarter earnings for fiscal 1998, causing them to be "below the restated $0.26 in the year-ago quarter," he said. "More favorable comparisons are expected in subsequent quarters."
The company said it restated earnings for fiscal 1996 due to previously announced accounting irregularities.

The materials maker on Wednesday reported fiscal 1997 sales of $278 million, up 17.7 percent from $236.2 million in fiscal 1996. Annual net income was $16.2 million, versus the previous year's restated net income of $8.5 million, including a $2.6-million after-tax restructuring charge.
Shares in the company were up 5/8 to 15.
